Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end collsiion sustained while turning left, with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache
consistent with cervical whiplash. The mechanism and force of impact reported are in keeping with the injury pattern
documented. Over the course of 28 visits, care consisted of spinal manipulation, therapeutic exercise, and soft tissue techniques,
following a typical progression. Frequency of visits decreased steadily as symptoms improved and range of motion returned.
Physical examination reveaeld reduced cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, supporting the clinical
diagnosis, while neuorlogical screening and reflex testing were within normal limits. The patient also reported a remote, minor
strain to the same region years earlier, which had resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing records reflect single,
appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no duplicate entries.
